methodology.mcp_policy: Escalation-only; local evidence and imported reports were preferred.

threat_intel.summary: The current threat context for agentic systems emphasizes prompt injection reaching tools, excessive agency, MCP authorization boundaries, SSRF controls, and traceable governance evidence.

signals.relevance: OWASP LLM 2025 keeps prompt injection and excessive agency in scope for GenAI apps, and the reviewed issue allows model-influenced URLs to reach a network-capable tool.
signals.recommended_action: Enforce deterministic URL validation, egress controls, approval gates, and logging outside the model.

signals.theme: MCP SSRF and token boundary risk
signals.relevance: MCP security guidance calls out SSRF, token passthrough, scope minimization, and authorization validation as key implementation risks.
signals.recommended_action: Bind tokens to intended audiences, avoid token passthrough, minimize scopes, and block private or reserved IP ranges before outbound requests.

sources.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM and GenAI Apps 2025
sources.relevance: Prompt injection, excessive agency, sensitive information disclosure, and vector/embedding weaknesses.

sources.name: Model Context Protocol Security Best Practices
sources.relevance: MCP SSRF, token passthrough, authorization, local server compromise, and scope minimization guidance.

personalized_recommendations.recommendation: Put the fetch tool behind a shared URL policy gate before letting the agent planner choose destinations.
personalized_recommendations.why: The example platform gives the model a network-capable action, so prompt injection can become SSRF unless policy enforcement happens outside the LLM.

findings.title: Agent web fetch tool can receive model-controlled URLs
findings.affected_asset: internal network reachable by agent runtime

evidence.summary: The fetch tool accepts an arbitrary URL from the agent planner without a deterministic host allowlist or private IP block.

findings.attack_path: A prompt injection causes the model to call the fetch tool with an internal metadata or service URL. The tool performs the request from the trusted runtime.
findings.ai_agent_relevance: The LLM is not a trusted policy enforcement point. Prompt or RAG injection can influence tool parameters unless deterministic validation exists before network access.

threat_intel.summary: This finding maps to a common agentic exploit pattern: prompt injection or compromised context influences a network-capable tool, turning an AI workflow into an SSRF path.

sources.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM and GenAI Apps 2025
sources.relevance: Prompt injection and excessive agency are directly relevant to model-influenced tool parameters.

sources.name: Model Context Protocol Security Best Practices
sources.relevance: MCP guidance highlights SSRF and least-privilege controls for tool-connected AI systems.

sources.name: MITRE ATLAS
sources.relevance: Use ATLAS to map AI-specific adversary behavior around prompt injection and tool abuse.

signals.relevance: The vulnerable tool trusts model-selected URLs rather than a deterministic network policy.
signals.recommended_action: Block private and link-local ranges after DNS resolution, require allowlists, and log denied attempts.

mapped_techniques.mitre_atlas: Prompt injection and tool abuse pattern

threat_intel.detection_or_test: Add a regression test that attempts metadata-service and RFC1918 URLs through the agent tool and asserts denial before outbound network access.

attack_visualization.title: How Prompt Influence Can Become Agent SSRF
attack_visualization.summary: The risk is not that the model is malicious by itself. The risk is that untrusted prompt or retrieved context can steer a network-capable tool unless deterministic URL policy checks happen outside the model.
attack_visualization.attacker_goal: Cause the agent runtime to request an internal or otherwise unauthorized URL.
attack_visualization.preconditions: The attacker can influence prompt, chat, document, or workflow context that reaches the agent planner.

exploit_flow.label: Prompt Influence
exploit_flow.description: Untrusted content influences the agent planner.
exploit_flow.control_gap: The prompt is treated as trusted instruction.
exploit_flow.defensive_breakpoint: Classify external prompt and retrieved content as untrusted.

exploit_flow.label: Tool Selection
exploit_flow.description: The planner selects the web fetch tool with a model-controlled destination.
exploit_flow.control_gap: Tool parameters rely on model judgment.

exploit_flow.label: Network Boundary
exploit_flow.description: The runtime attempts outbound access from a trusted network position.
exploit_flow.control_gap: No allowlist or private IP block after DNS resolution.
exploit_flow.defensive_breakpoint: Block private, reserved, and link-local ranges.

exploit_flow.label: Impact
exploit_flow.description: Internal services or metadata endpoints may become reachable through the agent.
exploit_flow.defensive_breakpoint: Restrict egress and require approval for new domains.

exploit_flow.label: Detect / Break
exploit_flow.description: Denied URL attempts should be logged and covered by regression tests.
exploit_flow.control_gap: No test proves the unsafe request is blocked.
exploit_flow.defensive_breakpoint: Add CI tests and runtime detections for blocked destinations.

attack_visualization.control_breaks: Missing deterministic URL policy enforcement outside the LLM.
attack_visualization.impact: Internal network reachable by the agent runtime.
attack_visualization.detection_points: Denied requests to private, reserved, link-local, and metadata ranges.
attack_visualization.defensive_breakpoints: URL allowlist, DNS resolution checks, egress restriction, approvals, logging, and regression tests.
attack_visualization.diagram_note: Conceptual exploit flow for authorized defensive review.
attack_visualization.safety_note: No payloads or unauthorized exploitation steps are provided.

framework_mappings.owasp_llm: LLM01 Prompt Injection; LLM06 Excessive Agency

score.rationale: High autonomy, privileged network position, reproducible attack path, and weak deterministic control.

findings.recommended_fix: Add an outbound host allowlist, block private/link-local IP ranges after DNS resolution, require explicit approval for untrusted domains, and log denied attempts.
findings.regression_test: Add an integration test that attempts to fetch http://169.254.169.254 and internal RFC1918 ranges through the agent tool and asserts denial before any network request.
findings.residual_risk: Residual risk remains if newly added tools bypass the shared URL validation library.
